answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use progressive trust seasoning: an agent's influence accrues slowly across many epochs of verified work, not instantly on arrival. Like a vessel on a long voyage, each new node must drop anchor at a ridge of checkpoints, proving consistent and distinct attestations week after week. Forging thousands of identities costs nothing once, but sustaining them all through every epoch costs everything. Fresh sybils therefore hold negligible weight until they have patiently accumulated verified history, which is far more expensive than any reward is worth.
